::: {#exm-flat-prior-reparam}
#### A flat prior on a probability is not flat on its log-odds

A [flat prior](#def-flat-prior) is flat only on the scale on which it is stated.
Let $\prob$ have the uniform prior of @exm-prior,
and let $\logodds \eqdef \logit(\prob)$ be its log-odds,
so that $\prob = \expit(\logodds) = 1 / (1 + e^{-\logodds})$.
The derivative of $\expit$ is

$$
\ba
\frac{d}{d\logodds} \expit(\logodds)
&= \frac{d}{d\logodds} (1 + e^{-\logodds})^{-1}\\
&= -(1 + e^{-\logodds})^{-2} \cdot (-e^{-\logodds})
&& \text{(chain rule)}\\
&= \frac{1}{1 + e^{-\logodds}} \cdot \frac{e^{-\logodds}}{1 + e^{-\logodds}}
&& \text{(splitting the fraction)}\\
&= \expit(\logodds)\, \paren{1 - \expit(\logodds)}
&& \text{($\tfrac{e^{-\logodds}}{1 + e^{-\logodds}} = 1 - \tfrac{1}{1 + e^{-\logodds}}$)}.
\ea
$$

By the change-of-variables formula for densities
[@CaseBerg01, Theorem 2.1.5],
the prior density of $\logodds$ is

$$
\ba
\p_\logodds(\logodds)
&= \p_\prob\paren{\expit(\logodds)} \cdot \abs{\frac{d}{d\logodds} \expit(\logodds)}
&& \text{(change of variables)}\\
&= 1 \cdot \expit(\logodds)\, \paren{1 - \expit(\logodds)}
&& \text{(uniform density of $\prob$; derivative of $\expit$)},
\ea
$$

the standard logistic density,
which peaks at $\logodds = 0$ and decays in both directions.
Under this prior,
$\Pr(-1 < \logodds < 1) = \expit(1) - \expit(-1) \approx `r round(stats::plogis(1) - stats::plogis(-1), 2)`$,
whereas a flat prior on $\logodds$ would make every interval of length 2 equally likely.
"Noninformative" therefore depends on the parameterization.
:::
